meta.title: iynk: a hardware lab in your browser
meta.description: An open source workbench for circuits, boards, robots and drones. Wire parts, write code, run it and break it on purpose, in your browser, with no account.

hero.title:
Learn hardware by wiring it,
running it and breaking it
hero.lede: iynk is an open source workbench for circuits, boards, robots and drones. Wire parts, write code, run it, and watch the simulation answer, all in your browser.
hero.reassure: No account. Nothing to install. Your work stays in this browser.
hero.proof: {boards} boards, {benches} robotics benches and {drones} drones, each one runnable.
hero.figure: Arduino Uno R3 running Blink on a breadboard, live: drag to turn it

tagline.text: Wire a part the wrong way and watch it fail. Fix it, and watch it work. That is when the datasheet finally makes sense.

see.title: See the circuit think
see.text: Turn a hand drawn 3D board, switch between breadboard and schematic, and watch the pins and the current change as the code runs.

code.title: Write code and get a result
code.text: Edit Arduino C++, MicroPython or Verilog and press Run. The simulation drives the figure, the pins and the serial monitor.

break.title: Break it, then learn why
break.text: Leave a resistor off, fit a part backwards, put a motor on the wrong pin. Each fault explains what failed and how to fix it.

fly.title: Fly what you built
fly.text: Size a drone with the thrust and weight maths, pass the safety tests, then fly it on a range against your best runs.

boards.text: From the Arduino Uno R3 to two FPGA boards: lessons, a live code editor, schematic and breadboard views, a serial monitor and failures that really trigger.

robotics.text: Motor drivers, sensors and power stages, built part by part with live status and current draw.

drones.text: From a Tiny Whoop to an octocopter: build it part by part, check the maths, pass the safety tests, then fly.

1.title: Pick a part
1.text: Choose a board, a robotics bench or a drone. Each opens as a figure you can turn and take apart.

2.title: Wire it and write code
2.text: Follow a lesson or start from Blink. The editor, the pinout and the serial monitor sit beside the figure.

3.title: Run it, then break it
3.text: Press Run. Switch on a fault, read the check that failed, fix it, and run it again.

proof.title: What runs, and what is simulated

runs.title: What runs in your browser
runs.1: Your Arduino C++, MicroPython and Verilog run in interpreters inside the page, on a fixed clock, so the same code gives the same result.
runs.2: Pins, the serial monitor and the figure answer your code.
runs.3: A circuit solver decides what a mistake does, and shows the current.

sim.title: What is simulated
sim.1: The parts follow models of their datasheets, not the real silicon.
sim.2: Timing follows the simulation clock, not a chip's.
sim.3: Your code is not compiled for the board.

proof.fidelity: iynk runs your code in its own interpreter, not on a real chip. It teaches how parts behave; it does not replace a bench, a compiler or a datasheet.

1.a: No. There is nothing to register for. Your progress and settings stay in this browser.

2.a: Yes. It is open source and has no paid tier. If you run your own copy, any AI or search keys you add are your own.

3.a: English, Spanish, French, German, Chinese and Hindi, including the labels inside the figures.

4.q: Does my code run on a real board?
4.a: No. It runs in iynk's own interpreter in the page. To use a real board you still need a compiler and a bench.

5.a: Parts follow simple models and the clock is deterministic. Treat the results as teaching, not as a test of your hardware.

6.q: What do the AI features need?
6.a: They are optional. Add your own key under Settings, Keys and usage, and the partner and the shop search switch on. Everything else works without one.

7.a: In this browser on this device. Clearing site data removes it.

8.q: Can I read or change the code?
8.a: Yes. The source is on GitHub, with a guide to running your own copy and one to contributing.

open.title: Open source
open.text: Read it, run your own copy, or send a fix.

end.title: The bench is ready.
end.text: Pick a board and press Run. There is nothing to install and no account to make.
